newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast spot prods ease, APIs viewed bearish.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast spot prods ease, APIs viewed bearish.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot refined products prices eased in quiet Tuesday trade and a report on regional inventories promised to weaken values further because of growing supplies, traders said.
West Coast gasoline supplies rose 539,000 barrels to stand 28.6 million for the week ended May 2, narrowing the year-on-year deficit to 310,000 barrels.
"That won't have anyone exciting to own gas," one trader said, noting few bidders came into the market Tuesday.
"Rack" prices for gasoline were stable while diesel fuel at distribution terminals eased about a cent Tuesday.
Conventional grade unleaded gasoline fell 0.50 cents a gallon from Monday to 60.50/61.50 cents.
CARB unleaded gasoline dropped 1.50 cents a gallon to 62.50/63.50 cents a gallon, with premium notionally talked five cents a gallon higher.
Jet fuel sold at 57.50 cents a gallon Tuesday, down a half cent from yesterday's average prices.
